resolutions.researcher_notes: Could NOT find a source supporting the recorded StartYear1=2023 -- and found positive disconfirming evidence instead, so per the standing rule (never propose refs for a different value) this is left UNRESOLVED rather than cited. This confirms and strengthens the prior deep-sweep audit's flag on this same row (rows/P5533.json validity concern), which cited a PNGRB Annual Report 2019-20 table from a cached local copy but could not re-locate a live URL for it within its search budget. I located and fetched that same document via the Wayback Machine this pass: https://web.archive.org/web/20220110141655if_/https://pngrb.gov.in/pdf/annualreports/eng2019-2020.pdf (curl-confirmed HTTP 200, verified as the genuine PNGRB Annual Report 2019-20 PDF; url_verifier.py FAILs on it with 'missing expected: Bhatinda' -- a false negative, matching this country's documented large-PDF keyword-match issue -- confirmed locally via pdftotext -layout instead). Its table '(B) Natural Gas Pipelines Partly Commissioned (As on 30 June, 2020)', row 5, Unique ID 5.02.NGPL, 'Bhatinda - Jammu - Srinagar', Entity GSPL India Gasnet Limited: Authorised Length 725 km, Authorised Capacity 42.42 MMSCMD (exact match to GEM's Capacity), Date of Authorisation 07.07.2011, 'Commissioned Length/ready for gas-in (Km)' = 102 (exact match to GEM's LengthKnown=102.00 for this Phase I row), Target date of Completion 24.02.2022, States Punjab/Jammu & Kashmir. If 102 km was already 'ready for gas-in' as of 30 June 2020, GEM's StartYear1=2023 for this same segment is off by roughly three years -- this is a material disagreement per the corroboration rule, not a source I can cite in support. I did NOT propose the archived document as a ref for Start[ref] because it contradicts rather than supports the recorded value; per the task's own instructions a value disagreement routes to Update, not a ref-sweep citation. Web search was unavailable for the rest of this pass (session WebSearch budget exhausted at 200/200), so I could not chase a GIGL/GSPL press release or news story specifically dated 2023 that might reconcile 'ready for gas-in' (mechanical completion, 2020) against actual commercial gas flow start (possibly later -- the current PNGRB MIS report, 20260531 edition, shows this segment's Gas Supplied at only 0.1 MMSCMD / 0.3% utilisation even now, which is at least consistent with a segment that sat mechanically complete but barely flowing gas for years, so a later 'first gas' date is plausible but I found nothing dated to confirm 2023 specifically). Recommend a future pass with search budget available chase a GIGL/GSPL India Gasnet investor disclosure, PNGRB tariff order, or CAG audit naming an actual commissioning/first-gas date for this segment, and route any correction through Update rather than this ref-sweep.
